A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work; v2 explicitly identifies InfGen as its earlier name. The main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original initial-state generation, motion prediction, and reinforcement-learning experiments in Section 3, plus WOSAC results in Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the WOSAC evaluation now presented in Section 3.5.

M1.justification: Tokenization, attention, prediction heads, kinematic rollout, and training objectives are retained. The state-forcing terminology clarifies persistent-agent state reconstruction already described in v1 Appendix D; the new FAQ does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use WOMD for the same generation, prediction, densification, and planner-learning tasks, alongside WOSAC 2025 evaluation. The WOSAC material moves from Appendix F to Section 3.5 without expanding coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain MotionCLIP, TrafficGen, LCTGen, UniGen variants, Log-Replay, and the same internal model variants. UniMM and CAT-K already appear in v1 Table 4 and remain the WOSAC comparators.

E3.justification: The established training and evaluation settings are retained, but v2 Appendix F newly states that densification uses 80 agents while Section 3.3 still specifies 128, as in v1. The PDFs do not resolve whether this reflects a different experiment, a setting revision, or a documentation error.

E4.justification: The autoregressive-decoding ablation, Motion-versus-Full comparison, adaptive-training and rejection-sampling comparisons, and qualitative failure examples are retained. The new FAQ supplies explanations rather than additional experimental analyses.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains identical uncertainty entries. Neither version specifies additional repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or an explanation of the reported plus/minus statistic.

E6.justification: All 22 numerical rows across Tables 1–4 match, including uncertainty values. For example, WOSAC realism remains 0.7731 and minADE remains 1.4252. The qualitative examples and reported behavioral findings are also retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, kinematic updates, attention equations, and coordinate transformations retain their substance. Equation 5 clarifies the SOS token's role alongside the same eight state attributes; no new theory, assumptions, proofs, or derivations appear.

C1.justification: The introduction removes the claim that this is the first framework using a single autoregressive model for initial states and trajectories. The central claims about continuous generation, dynamic agent populations, versatility, and downstream planner benefits remain.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 and the new FAQ explicitly explain why reconstructing continuing agents' states does not introduce ground-truth leakage. The limitations paragraph narrows the resource concern from general memory and compute demands to training memory. Existing performance interpretations and failure cases remain.

D1.justification: The FAQ adds implementation disclosures about incremental agent IDs, generation termination, suppressing the end-token logit, and prescribing agent counts by category. The project-information link changes. Architecture, preprocessing, training hyperparameters, and hardware specifications were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B substantially revise novelty positioning by acknowledging SceneDiffuser's unified initialization and rollout and comparing against concurrent Interleaved InfGen. They distinguish map-anchored token groups from ego-centric representations and add SceneDiffuser++, UniScene, and related discussion, replacing a broader claim of unique unification with specific technical distinctions.

P1.justification: The paper renames InfGen to SceneStreamer, refines terminology, and edits or condenses several paragraphs while preserving most text and section organization. WOSAC discussion moves into Section 3.5, and Appendix F becomes a new FAQ.

P2.justification: The four tables and nine figures are retained, with model-label and caption edits. Table 4 moves from the appendix into the main text. The ICLR template changes headers, typography, and placement of existing exhibits without substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 improves inference clarity and gives more careful novelty positioning through explicit comparisons with other unified simulators. The FAQ adds useful reproducibility information while preserving the empirical evidence. Its unresolved 80-versus-128-agent inconsistency limits these gains, but the overall improvement in clarity and positioning is supported.
